output.final_rationale: The verdict does not change. No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor expressly offered none and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is partially valid in one respect: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not by themselves satisfy the governing policy when the affected segment remains exposed. But that concession does not improve the compliance outcome. The policy text is explicit that rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. On the available evidence summary, neither condition is met. This is the key distinction between a narrowed caveated position and actual compliant certification: a caveat can prevent overstatement, but it cannot satisfy an unresolved compliance predicate. Because the certification claim still depends on conditions not shown by admissible evidence, the current record remains noncompliant.
